title: Environmental groups call for stop to orbital datacentres
text:
## 事件
美国多个环保组织（EarthJustice、DarkSky International等）联合向FCC提交请愿，要求对轨道数据中心提案进行严格环境审查，警告其可能带来不可逆的生态损害。请愿指出包括SpaceX在内的企业计划发射超过100万颗太空数据中心卫星，但FCC历来未进行环境评估。

## 影响
轨道数据中心项目面临监管不确定性上升，可能导致商业发射及运营进程延期。太空计算相关产业（卫星制造、发射服务、太空芯片设计）的预期增速可能受环保压力抑制。

## 标的线索
- SpaceX（待核实，太空数据中心核心提出方）
- Orbital Compute（待核实，计划建设10万颗卫星、10吉瓦算力的太空AI计算星座）
- 意法半导体（待核实，其高管曾将轨道数据中心视为未来三年内的相关市场机会）
- 卫星及空间通信相关板块（待核实）

## 待验证
- 环保组织请愿后FCC的具体回应时间与态度
- 轨道数据中心项目当前的商业推进阶段及主要参与方实际发射计划
- 轨道数据中心是否已进入实际工程落地阶段，还是仍处于概念提案期

prompt_system:
你是「资讯雷达」投研向改写助手。任务：把用户提供的一篇资讯压成可读的投研草稿。

硬性要求：
1. 严格用下面四个中文小节标题（Markdown ##），顺序固定，每节 1-4 条短句：
## 事件
## 影响
## 标的线索
## 待验证
2. 只客观陈述；不推荐买卖；不预测涨跌；不构成投资建议。
3. 「标的线索」只能写可能相关的公司/板块/主题，并标注「待核实」；没有则写「暂无明确标的线索」。
4. 「待验证」写需要交叉核对的事实或缺口；没有则写「暂无」。
5. 不要输出前后缀寒暄、不要编造文中不存在的数字。

Highlighting a threat of “irreparable environmental harm to our planet”, they say the FCC must provide both oversight and conduct a thorough review of the risks and impacts of the projects The coalition states that companies, including SpaceX, are making plans to launch more than a million such datacentres into space. The group consists of EarthJustice filing the petition on behalf of DarkSky International, Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility, and Environment America. Pollution and debris “Allowing a million orbiting datacentres with no environmental review isn’t just irresponsible – it’s reckless,” said Tim Whitehouse, executive director of Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility. “The potential for these projects to degrade the atmosphere with pollution and debris and harm wildlife needs to be carefully considered before licensing these projects.” “These projects could permanently alter the night sky as we know it,” said Ruskin Hartley, executive director of DarkSky International. “The FCC needs to take seriously its obligation to ensure these projects do not cause unnecessary harm to naturally dark skies, or to our overall environment.” They report the number of satellites in space has grown exponentially in recent years. From 1,400 active satellites, in 2015, to 15,000 in 2026. The number is projected to grow to an additional 58,000 by 2030. “Drastically expanding satellites in space has a direct impact on people’s everyday lives as well as the future of our planet,” said Jan Hasselman, senior attorney at Earthjustice. “Agencies that authorise companies looking to space as the next frontier still must operate within the law, and the law requires the FCC to consider all the risks and impacts of these proposals. If we have to sue so that they comply, we will.” FCC The group claims that the FCC has historically authorised satellites without any environmental review. And that it has also has never considered cumulative impacts. They list the environmental impacts of satellites and these include the following: emissions from rocket launches and reentries, debris from potential collisions, degradation of the ozone layer, and light pollution that would harm wildlife and negatively affect humans. Space compute Only this week, for example, the space startup Orbital Compute was reportedly preparing for a 100,000-satellite constellation of orbital datacentres to provide AI computing power in space. At full scale, it claims, the constellation would deliver approximately 10 gigawatts of compute. This would be without drawing on terrestrial electricity, land, or water. Previously, ST’s envisaged orbital datacentres becoming a reality within a few years. Remi El-Ouazzane, President of the Microcontrollers, Digital ICs & RF Products Group at ST – and a member of ST’s Executive Committee – saw them as a “ possible future market ” that could reach “relevant amounts” in about three years time. You can read the EarthJustice petition online.
